speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The Bill has been put together after a holistic review of the Community Disputes Management Framework, or CDMF in short.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In doing so, we have also consulted extensively with the public and other stakeholders.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This included more than 30 focus group discussions with members of the public, academics as well as frontline personnel.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This move will strengthen our ability to bring neighbours together, in an amicable environment to discuss their differences and understand each other's perspectives.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Mediation is quick, it will be made free and thus far, has proven effective.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will therefore strengthen this framework to encourage neighbour disputes to be amicably resolved, as a measure of first resort.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: CRU officers will have a range of investigatory and enforcement powers to intervene in neighbour disputes.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This includes the power to issue advisories, warnings and abatement orders.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The CRU will focus on addressing severe noise and hoarding disamenity cases.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: A substantial proportion of neighbour dispute cases involve noise disamenity.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This will plug an existing gap where agencies do not presently have sufficient powers to intervene, to more effectively deal with some individuals who are seriously disrupting the community harmony with their behaviour.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: By and large, once this new framework becomes fully operational, we expect most of the disamenity cases to be addressed by the mediation enhancements, or by the CRU framework that we will put in place.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: There will, however, be a small fraction of cases that will be harder to resolve, where parties might be intransigent and where the issues at hand might have become deep-rooted.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: By the time these cases get to the CDRT, these cases will need to be managed quickly and effectively.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will therefore revise the CDRT framework to enable this.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In my speech, Sir, I will first set out our overall approach to managing community disputes.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And thereafter, explain the details which underpin each of the three areas of enhancements.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: My colleague, Senior Minister of State for National Development Sim Ann, will be overseeing the CRU powers under the new Part 2A.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: She will share more details on the CRU framework and directed mediation by frontline officers in her speech.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: When individuals, most of us, live close to one another, some degree of friction will inevitably arise.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: On average, that is around 2,500 complaints every month, or over 80 complaints every day.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Noise complaints, by far, form the vast majority of all neighbour disputes feedback received by agencies.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Most complaints, not surprisingly, come from Housing and Development Board (HDB) estates – since around 80% of our population reside in HDB estates.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But having said that, we are not unique in having this problem.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Other cities around the world face similar issues.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In the United Kingdom (UK), for example, it has been reported that at least two in five people have had disagreements with their neighbours.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And like in Singapore, noise disamenity is the top cause of disputes in the UK.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In 2014, we formalised our approach for managing neighbour disputes under the umbrella of the CDMF.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: That was when we first set up the CDMF.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The CDMF seeks to promote good relations among neighbours to minimise the occurrence of disputes.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, it is not just a question of dealing with the disamenity, but how do we go upstream to manage the conflict at an early stage.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It also seeks to encourage neighbours to resolve issues amicably among themselves when such disputes arise.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It helps to promote community mediation as the primary source of assistance if neighbours need to resolve their differences, and it provides for the CDRT, as an avenue of last resort.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, as a primary starting point, I want to emphasise to Members in this House, that even as we introduce this Bill to substantially strengthen the CDMF framework, our aim remains building a strong, resilient and cohesive community where neighbours are friendly with one another, they are more likely to be tolerant and understanding.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And they will then, in turn, be more open to discussing minor annoyances which may arise and then aiming to constructively address them without escalation.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We have thus far, taken steps to foster a shared understanding of community norms among residents when it comes to noise.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In 2022, MND brought together representatives from various sectors and set up the Community Advisory Panel on Neighbourhood Noise, or CAP in short.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: More than 4,400 members of the public, participated in CAP's engagements.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Many agreed that the first step in managing noise disputes should be communication with neighbours.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The CAP also highlighted the importance of practising considerate behaviour.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It highlighted some simple, but sometimes we take for granted, practical steps that residents can take in their day to day living.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: For example, using door stoppers to prevent the accidental slamming of windows and doors.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Or closing the windows when engaging in noisy activities, like karaoke and other such pursuits that one might enjoy at home.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Since then, MND has worked with the Singapore Kindness Movement and agencies like HDB to promote the community norms and encourage considerate behaviour.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Despite this, occasionally, I think we have all come across in each of our constituency occasions where disputes between neighbours will arise.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These disputes do not usually raise law-and-order issues.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, it is not a matter for the Police.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Instead, these disputes usually, though not always, stem from differences in lifestyles, schedules, depending on working schedules, preferences at home.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We might have parents with young energetic children – nothing wrong with that – but they live next to teenagers preparing for exams or the elderly who might need their rest at an earlier hour in the day.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The laughter of children may bring joy to many but, in some situations or occasions it is an intrusion on peace and tranquility.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Nothing wrong with the needs of both sides but, sometimes, finding that common ground to alleviate this dispute is a challenge.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: When such disputes arise, our guiding principle has been that neighbours should proactively and constructively engage with one another and try to reach a workable compromise.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: If they are unable to do so themselves, they should seek assistance from a community mediator.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Mediators at the Community Mediation Centre, or CMC for short, have deep experience in facilitating effective dialogue between disputing neighbours and encouraging them to find common ground.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This, we feel, and continue to feel even with the new CDMF framework, is the best way to resolve a dispute between neighbours.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It is non-confrontational, it preserves the long-standing relationship as far as possible and, overall, maintains harmony in society.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Indeed, as an Asian society, amicable resolution is not unknown.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Respected elders in the community in the past, like village headmen or clan or religious leaders, used to help in this process.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They stepped in, lowered temperatures, heard both sides, found common ground.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But I think the underlying principles of amicable resolution through discussion and compromise remain just as relevant, if not more, relevant today.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Indeed, many neighbour disputes have been resolved in this way and that was one of the considerations we took into account as we formulated the enhancements in this Bill.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Many of the remaining disputes are resolved after neighbours attend mediation at the CMC.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, we know that conciliation is effective in resolving community disputes.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It saves time and cost and, as I said, preserves the longer-term goodwill in the relationship.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And so, this has remained the guiding philosophy with which we have approached the proposed enhancements to the CDMF framework in this Bill.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, let me start on the three buckets of enhancements with mediation.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The first part of the enhancements is straightforward.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Today, we have often heard of many cases where one or both sides refused to engage in mediation even though we might think that is the best option for them.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They might refuse to consider mediation for a variety of reasons.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Some are personal ones, some perhaps may be ill-conceived ones.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Or they register for mediation, but then do not show up.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The new directed mediation powers will strengthen our ability to address such cases.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It will enable us to bring neighbours together for a good discussion in a non-confrontational space, at the CMC or perhaps some other agreed venue, and coming together is a critical step in finding a solution to resolving a dispute.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, Sir, under the new section 13M that is inserted under clause 14, authorised persons, such as a community relations officer or an officer from the CMC, may issue a Mediation Direction to individuals involved in a complaint or dispute involving alleged unreasonable interference.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Public officers or officers from a statutory body, such as HDB, can also be appointed to issue Mediation Directions.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Parties who receive a Mediation Direction must attend mediation at the CMC.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The statutory thresholds for Mediation Directions to be issued under section 13M have been deliberately kept low.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Authorised officers, such as HDB officers, may issue these Directions if there is a complaint or dispute involving neighbours, and that complaint or dispute relates to alleged unreasonable interference.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Officers are not required to conduct detailed fact-finding to determine who is right or who is wrong, or, indeed, the nature or extent of the alleged nuisance.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The role of these frontline officers, as first responders to a community dispute, is not to determine fault in that first instance, but to bring the neighbours together for open dialogue and, if need be, through a Mediation Direction.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As I mentioned earlier, mediation at CMC is quick and effective.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Our statistics have shown that, today, more than 80% of voluntary mediation cases at the CMC are settled amicably.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These are cases, of course, where the parties had agreed to attend mediation and did attend meditation.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We might, therefore, expect to see the settlement rates become lower once directed mandatory mediation takes place.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But if we can even help more neighbours to make peace through a consensual, amicable arrangement, that is still a good outcome.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And even if after going through the process, mediation were to be unsuccessful in that it did not result in a compromise or an amicable solution, time, I think, is not wasted.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Parties would have heard each other’s perspectives and this can help to lay the groundwork for eventual resolution.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Next, Sir, as we strengthen the ability to foster open dialogue between parties, we should also give more "bite" to the settlement agreements that parties enter into, after a successful mediation.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, under the new section 31A, we sought to strike a balance.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This helps to facilitate quicker and simpler recourse if registered settlements are breached.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And in such situations, I would hope that neighbours, disputing parties, need not be trigger-happy to always seek enforcement applications in the first instance.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They can sometimes inquire with their neighbours as to why or how such an order came to be breached or an agreement came to be breached and I would say if you can speak to your neighbour first, there is a good chance you might then find a way to reach a compromise and resolve the matter, having already done so once.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The simpler Court enforcement process is there to ensure that, if it is indeed breached and there is no subsequent solution found, then, thereafter, the relief can be quick and expeditious.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But that, really, I would encourage as a measure of last resort in this case.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This is the second bucket of enhancements to the CDMF.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But at the same time, they are severely disrupting community peace.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: For example, we have heard of cases where a neighbour deliberately disrupts the peace by banging loudly on the walls or the ceilings throughout the day and, even sometimes, in the middle of the night continuously.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: There are also cases where the acts might not be deliberate or consciously deliberate.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But the community nonetheless suffers disamenity, impacting harmony and quality of life and, sometimes we see severe hoarding cases as some examples.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Fortunately, at this point in time, these cases are still in the small minority.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But if left unaddressed, they can escalate and, thereafter, have an outsized impact on the community.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, we are thinking of how we can pre-emptively disrupt this.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Today, agencies do not have sufficient powers to effectively address them.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We have considered this carefully and also studied what other countries have done.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Under the new Part 2A, the Bill proposes for CRU officers to have a range of powers to investigate, take decisive action in neighbour disputes that involve unreasonable interference, and this includes the kinds of cases that I have given examples of.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Officers may investigate, for example, by taking statements from neighbours or taking photographs and recordings, which can then have evidential value.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This can help ameliorate cases which very often we see descend into a "he said/she said there is this noise at that time" or "this volume and that volume".

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I think this helps to cut through all that and allows objective statements and evidence to be taken.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: After investigations are completed, officers may issue advisories or warnings, as appropriate.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These warnings or advisories do not carry penalties, in the first instance.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But if they are not heeded, then an abatement order under section 13L may be issued subsequently.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: An abatement order can require the recipient to stop any acts that are causing unreasonable interference to surrounding neighbours and it will be an offence under section 13L subsection 5 to disobey an abatement order without reasonable excuse.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I hope we do not always have to resort to issuing an abatement order.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Sometimes, the mere presence of a uniformed officer with powers will be sufficient in itself to abate certain behaviours.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Other times, a warning may then have to be issued.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Over time, Sir, we hope to see this framework have a salutary effect or a self-moderating impact on both the community and individual residents.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The community will know the boundaries, and then begin to self-police.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Senior Minister of State Sim Ann will expand on the details on the new CRU.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But before I leave the topic, let me explain the thinking behind the role of the CRU and the scope of its powers.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The statutory powers that will be conferred on the CRU in this Bill under the new Part 2A have been drafted to cover a range of matters.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These are matters which usually cause community disputes.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They can cover a wide range of acts or omissions, which can lead to unreasonable interference with a neighbour’s enjoyment or use of place of residence and this is intended to cater for flexibility in the CRU's deployment to allow it to do its work effectively.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: However, it is not intended for the CRU to become the first responder in all cases, and that is simply not possible.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As I explained earlier, this noise, in particular, forms the vast majority of neighbour disamenity complaints and we have got to balance resources against what impact can be felt in the community and how we feel these resources best make a difference to resolving disputes between neighbours.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The CRU will, of course, have discretion to judge the severity of these matters and cases, having regard to the specific facts and circumstances of each case, and we will reflect this in subsidiary legislation made under section 13Z read with section 13G.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It is, therefore, not our intention in this Bill to be overly prescriptive.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: CRU Officers will assess on a case-by-case basis and have the ability to make a judgement call.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In general, due to the transitory nature of noise, a case would be considered severe only if it persists over a period of time.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But, in some cases, a single occurrence might well possibly be treated as severe.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: For example, if a person deliberately takes a drill to his wall or ceiling at 3.00 am, in the middle of the night with the intent of waking up his neighbours, then HDB officers might well look into this the next day and, if it happens again, the CRU may treat it as "severe".

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I would also like to caution that we must strike a balance between the CRU stepping in to manage a dispute and also at the same time leaving enough room for neighbours to settle their private disputes between themselves.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I think we have to strike that balance very judiciously and very carefully.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: If we intervene too much, we take away the community's ability to self-police and self-moderate, which is the essence of really good neighbourliness.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: With the CRU framework, the Government is already taking a significant step forward, to lean forward to help to resolve these cases, particularly if they threaten to have a wider negative impact on the community.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Fundamentally though, we believe that most neighbour disputes ought to be addressed by strengthening the community in the manner that I have outlined earlier and creating an overdependence on the state to police community behaviours at home will invariably weaken the community’s ability to self-moderate.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In addition, we must be prudent with how we spend our limited resources and manpower.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And I think Members can appreciate that, for a matter like this, for the CRU to be stepping in on those occasions with the kinds of cases and the volume of cases or noise that I have outlined, it is very resource-intensive.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And this is a substantial endeavour, both in terms of resources as well as manpower.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The learnings from this pilot will help us understand how to effectively scale up these operations and make it effective and efficient island-wide.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: During the CRU pilot in Tampines, grassroots leaders and frontline agencies will continue existing efforts to manage neighbour disputes, both in Tampines as well as applying in the rest of Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Senior Minister of State Sim Ann will share more details on the CRU.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I move on, Sir, to the third bucket of enhancements in this Bill, which is the CDRT.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We intend, as I said earlier, for the CDRT to remain an avenue of last resort.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I mentioned earlier that many difficult noise and hoarding cases should be addressed by directed mediation enhancements or by the CRU framework.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We are hopeful that, eventually, only a small fraction of cases will remain unresolved after these layers of upstream intervention.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: By the time we get to this stage, however, these cases are likely to be quite severe and protracted, involving a recalcitrant party.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will therefore enhance the CDRT's processes and powers; and equip it to deliver quicker and more effective relief.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Some of the CDRT enhancements will also go towards supporting upstream amicable resolution efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This, I think, is just the flip side of imposing mandatory mediation.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, we think that there is a reservoir of cases out there that will benefit from mandatory mediation, even on the existing framework as it currently exists.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And this is not what we want to see.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We accept that there may be some cases that could not or may not be suitable for mediation – and there is, therefore, flexibility in section 18A to waive pre-filing mediation for such cases.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But, by and large, I would say residents should go for mediation first.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It is always better for parties to agree on an arrangement that both are comfortable with and both are prepared to abide by, than for a third party to adjudicate and then direct what one party can or cannot do.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This, in the long term, leads to more lasting peace in the community.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This brings the CRU process closer to the CDRT, if necessary.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This will help to alleviate the evidential difficulty highlighted by a number of CDRT users.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They often tell us when we conduct our focus groups discussions and take feedback, "How do we gather evidence of noise which is transient or transitory, and how do we ensure that when we get to the CDRT, we can establish the provenance of that piece of evidence".

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, we decided that we would bring the process of the CDRT closer to that of the evidence collected by the CRU.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In the proposed new framework, therefore, if the CRU had previously looked into the case, and a CDRT claim is thereafter filed, then the evidence gathered – such as observations, noise sensor data, statements from neighbours or previously-issued warnings and compliance or non-compliance therewith – can be submitted to the CDRT, for consideration.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This is so that claimants need not start all over again to prove their cases afresh.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They will not need to gather evidence from ground zero that CRU officers had already gathered and which they possess.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This will also help the CDRT come to a fair decision in a shorter period of time.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: MTOs can be issued if the CDRT has reason to believe that the respondent's acts of unreasonable interference stem, at least in part, from an underlying psychiatric condition.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Such a condition sometimes causes a person to disrupt the community, with noise or even hoarding, sometimes even unknowingly.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In those cases, the issue therefore is not just a disamenity one.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Hence, the MTO is intended to address the root cause of certain acts that a resident may engage in.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Our priority will remain to persuade the resident to voluntarily go for treatment.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And I want to emphasise that a CDRT-issued MTO will be a measure of last resort, taking into account the circumstances.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Members will see that the Bill provides for a robust framework to ensure that MTOs are issued only in deserving and appropriate cases.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And I think it is worth outlining the framework to Members in some detail.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Under section 12A subsection 1, the claimant must first establish that the respondent has caused unreasonable interference.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Next, the CDRT must have reasonable grounds to believe that the respondent is likely suffering from a psychiatric condition; and the psychiatric condition is likely contributing to the acts of unreasonable interference.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, there must be a nexus between the behaviour or the suspected behaviour and the interference.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: There is an On-site Psychiatrist Scheme in the State Courts to facilitate this assessment.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: After both conditions are met, the CDRT must, under subsection 8, call for a formal assessment from an appointed psychiatrist.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The respondent may also submit a report from a psychiatrist of his choice, and the CDRT can only make a MTO if the formal assessment report certifies certain matters – such as the respondent's suitability for treatment.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These measures ensure that improper applications are dismissed early, so that the party is not put through the course of the proceedings unnecessarily.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It also ensures that MTOs are only made in appropriate cases.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Clause 21 of the Bill repeals and replaces section 25 and clause 27(c) expands the existing rule-making power on costs.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: At present, Members may know that other than disbursements, costs cannot be awarded in CDRT proceedings.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will amend this and align with the general costs position under the Rules of Court 2021.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In particular, the CDRT will be able to award costs to self-represented persons, on the usual costs principles.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This compensates him for the time and work required for the proceedings.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We also intend to make subsidiary legislation to the effect that costs can be awarded against a party who did not make efforts at amicable resolution.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This will include situations where a resident declined an invitation from his neighbour to attend voluntary mediation, without good reason.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, in other words, even before you invoke mandatory mediation, if a neighbour approaches one party to offer voluntary mediation outside of this rubric and one unreasonably refuses to take up the offer, the Courts at the CDRT can take this into account when considering the cost orders to be made.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The intention, ultimately, is to encourage dispute resolution at the earliest possible opportunity.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And it would be best if neighbours go for mediation voluntarily – and not just wait for a Mediation Direction to be issued.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This will help claimants with serious cases to obtain relief more quickly, even as they wait for their cases to make their way through the process of the CDRT.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Even though we have expedited it, there might be some occasions where the disamenity of the interference is pressing and severe.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We have heard feedback that some landlords adopt a "hands-off" approach, refusing to intervene even after being informed and being made aware that their tenants are causing a nuisance.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The landlord must then act to abate the nuisance from his tenant.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: If the nuisance is not abated, and the affected resident succeeds on a CDRT claim, then the CDRT can make an order against the tenant.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And if the tenant does not comply, then the Court may forfeit all, or part of, the landlord's bond.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This effectively brings forward the existing compliance bond that can currently already be made against a landlord.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: There is already a provision for such a landlord's bond in the current framework.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It empowers the affected resident, under these amendments, to involve the landlord at an early stage, and this improves the chances of an amicable resolution in these cases.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Next, while mediation should be the first resort, there can be exceptional situations where it is necessary for the case to be brought before the CDRT.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: For example, there may be a protracted dispute between neighbours, where both parties, for example, could agree on the specific noise event, such as children playing in the corridor or making noise beyond a certain level and so on.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But they may disagree strongly on whether that constitutes unreasonable interference.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Or parties may have tried for some time, and there is evidence of that, but are unable to resolve this through other means, after multiple rounds of mediation, and they keep looking to CRU to make an intervention or make a finding, whilst at the same time, both parties themselves refuse to submit the case to CDRT for adjudication.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In such cases, by way of example, the DG of the CRU may bring this to the CDRT for resolution and the CDRT can require disputing residents to attend Court and examine the dispute, before making orders.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Along with that, the CDRT will be empowered, under the new section 5B, to vary an order, if there is a change in the personal circumstances of the applicant and it is just and equitable to do so.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: For example, when the original terms are no longer workable.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The CDRT may also vary its order to address situations where respondents attempt to circumvent the original order.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Next, the CDRT processes are designed to be simple, judge-led and accessible.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And with these amendments, we intend for it to be more so.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But this also raises the possibility of abuse.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Once you set the bar too low, it is easy to access, and people file claims easily.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And just like we come across occasions where our residents complain to us of a disamenity of a neighbour, you may also have heard of the shoe being on the other foot, where the neighbour comes to us to complain that they are unreasonable complaints or calls to the Police or calls to HDB being made by the neighbour.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: For example, if a person makes two or more applications that are totally without merit or are an abuse of process, then the CDRT can restrain the person from making further applications, unless permission is granted.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These are all, as a consequence of the enhancements that I have outlined.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The CMC Act is amended to support the new directed mediation framework.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The amendments also clarify that community mediation may be conducted by virtual means, like video conferencing and this adds to the convenience of parties attending mediation.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The Housing and Development Act is amended to enable HDB to consider compulsory acquisition of HDB flats in egregious cases – and Senior Minister of State Sim Ann will expand on this point later.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The Police Force Act is amended to repeal the existing community warden powers under sections 65C and 65D.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This is because it is no longer required, with the creation of the CRU.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Other consequential amendments are made under clauses 30, 38 and 39 of this Bill.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I hope that the enhancements under this Bill will address many of the cases that are escalated to agencies every year – and you heard the numbers earlier.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: For example, cases where neighbours are unwilling to take the first step to engage with one another, or for one reason or another, refuse to do so.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Or cases where the neighbourly relationship has deteriorated to the point where a person is deliberately disrupting the community peace, sometimes to get back at the neighbour.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Or cases where CDRT claimants find it difficult, when they go through the process, having had mediation, but failed – and the case is protracted, it is intransigent, it is severe, but you go through a process where you then have to lead evidence afresh, almost from ground zero again.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: All that, we try and change and improve with these sets of amendments.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: At the same time, Sir, I wish very much to emphasise that these enhancements cannot be seen as a silver bullet – they are not a panacea, they are not a silver bullet, they cannot address everyone's disputes and ills between neighbours.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: There will likely be cases that will continue to resist resolution, even under this enhanced framework.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We will play two roles in supporting the enhanced CDMF.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: As the Minister-in-charge of MSO, I will therefore be speaking on Part 2A of the Bill which deals with the operationalisation of the Community Relations Unit, or CRU for short, and allows Community Relations Officers and officers appointed by the Minister to issue Mediation Directions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The CRU will comprise the Director-General (DG) as well as other authorised officers to be appointed by the Minister, and the Community Relations Officers and Auxiliary Community Relations Officers appointed by the DG, or CROs and ACROs for short.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I will speak on the types of cases CRU will take on, the powers this Bill will equip it with, how it will intervene and the safeguards we will put in place.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I will also share an update on our plans to pilot the CRU, starting in Tampines.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I will then speak about the issuance of Mediation Directions by frontline officers, which HDB will pilot, also starting in Tampines.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Minister Edwin Tong earlier stated that the CRU will focus only on severe neighbour noise and hoarding cases.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The two main archetypes of severe noise cases that CRU will focus on are: one, severe and prolonged cases, where noise is being used to cause suffering to the surrounding neighbours; and two, cases where the acts that cause noise could be due to an underlying mental health condition.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Let us say there are two neighbours who live next to each other in Tampines town – Mr X and Mr Y.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr X reports that Mr Y has been making intense banging noises from late night to early morning for the past 10 years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: However, Mr X is unable to provide agencies with clear evidence that the noises are caused by Mr Y.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: According to Mr X, Mr Y tends to play a "cat and mouse" game.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: He stops banging when officers visit, but resumes banging right after officers leave.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In such a case, CROs may exercise their powers under the new section 13I and take statements from Mr X, Mr Y and surrounding neighbours.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: They may also require Mr Y to attend interviews.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: If Mr X wishes for CROs to deploy noise sensors and the relevant Town Council agrees, CROs may also deploy noise sensors in Mr X's unit, as well as along the common corridor to collect objective evidence of the reported noise, to measure its intensity and triangulate where it is most likely to be coming from.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Subsequently, if CROs are satisfied that Mr Y is indeed engaging in acts that are deliberately disrupting the peace of the neighbours throughout the day and night, then a written warning may be issued to Mr Y, which warns him to cease making the noise with immediate effect.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: If Mr Y does not comply with the abatement order to stop, then that will be a criminal offence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The DG may also seize the item that Mr Y used to cause the noise.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We will equip CRU officers with powers to carry out their tasks and also put in appropriate safeguards.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: First, under the new section 13E, before exercising any power, CROs and ACROs must identify themselves by showing their official identification card.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Members of the public will be able to go to an MND webpage, to verify that the person standing before them, is indeed from the CRU.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Impersonation of a CRU officer will be a criminal offence under section 13Q.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Next, under the new section 13I, CROs will have powers to take statements, photographs and recordings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: These are standard powers for public officers who perform enforcement functions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: However, if they are not heeded, further enforcement action may be taken.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: CROs will also have powers to issue Mediation Directions under section 13M.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Minister Edwin Tong explained this in detail earlier.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Under section 13L, the DG can issue an abatement order to an individual, if he is satisfied that the individual is engaging in an act or omission that causes unreasonable interference.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is modelled on what countries such as the UK and Australia have done.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: An abatement order requires the recipient to stop any acts that are causing unreasonable interference to their neighbours.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The recipient can also be required to take steps to ensure that other persons in the home, such as family members, stop the acts which are specified in the order.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: CROs will also be empowered to leverage on technology to do their work.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In particular, under sections 13I and 13J, CROs, assisted by ACROs, may deploy noise sensors to collect objective evidence on matters, such as the direction, timing and intensity of the noise nuisance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This addresses a gap today, where complainants attempt to collect evidence by making simple audio recordings, often on their mobile phones.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: These recordings are unable to tell us the intensity or direction of the noise disturbance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: They can also easily be distorted upon playback or edited and therefore cannot be relied upon for official investigations or court proceedings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The deployment of noise sensors gives us a sensible alternative to deploying officers on long and possibly futile stakeouts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We also hope sensors can deliver evidence in cases where the nuisance-maker stops the noise when officers are present but starts making noise again once the officers have left.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In relation to the deployment of noise sensors, I would like to assure Members there will be safeguards to protect residents' privacy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: These safeguards incorporate feedback from the public engagements that we have conducted.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: So, if the sensor is to be installed in someone's home, then the owner or occupier of the home must grant consent.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: If the sensor is to be installed in the common areas, then CRU must seek consent from the managing agent of the common area.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In the course of public consultations, some members of public suggested that CRU should be empowered to deploy noise sensors without obtaining consent, for example, within the home of a suspected noise-maker.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We considered this carefully but decided that it is not necessary to take this step for now.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Strict access controls will be placed on these servers and the raw data will be automatically expunged once it has been processed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Only processed data will be retained for the purposes of CRU's investigation and any subsequent court proceedings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This processed data will provide objective, untampered evidence on the direction, timing and intensity of the noise events above an ambient baseline.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The actual sounds, including any conversations that were picked up by the sensor, will not be available to our officers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: As a deterrent and an absolute last resort, for the most severe of cases that involve recalcitrant nuisance-makers, CRU may refer the matter to HDB after exhausting other levers, for HDB to consider compulsory acquisition.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: HDB has compulsory acquisition powers which have been used very sparingly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We recognise that it is a very severe action, which would affect not only the nuisance-maker but also the rest of the person's household.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We will not take this course of action without due care and consideration.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: HDB may consider compulsory acquisition of the flats of severe and recalcitrant nuisance-makers, if, for example, the owner or an occupier has been convicted by the Courts at least twice for disobeying an abatement order or a CDRT exclusion order.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The second noise scenario that CRU will focus on involves persons who may have mental health conditions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For example, let us consider a case where a resident who lives on his own has been shouting to himself for extended periods of time, even late at night.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The surrounding neighbours inform CRU that the resident might have an underlying mental health condition, as suggested by his behaviour.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For cases with mental health conditions, the aim will be to facilitate assessment, confirmation and treatment of the mental health condition.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In this case, CROs will work with partner agencies, such as the Agency for Integrated Care, the Institute of Mental Health (IMH) and the Police, to facilitate assessment, confirmation and treatment of the underlying mental health condition.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: If all attempts to persuade the resident to voluntarily seek mental health treatment fail, then, as a last resort, the DG may make an application to the CDRT under the new section 17A.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: If the CDRT is satisfied that the resident has indeed engaged in acts of unreasonable interference and the CDRT has reason to believe that the resident is likely suffering from a psychiatric condition that is contributing to his behaviour, then the CDRT may exercise the mandatory treatment powers under the new section 12A.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: While the volume of cases is not high, it is an issue that not only causes dis-amenities, but also poses public health and safety risks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It affects not only the hoarder, but also surrounding neighbours.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In severe hoarding cases, the home may be infested with pests due to rotting food.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The accumulation of clutter is also a potentially fatal fire hazard, as occupants may be unable to escape if a fire should break out.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The pests and stench may prevent surrounding neighbours from the normal enjoyment of their own homes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The root causes of a hoarder’s behaviour are complex.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: They could be due to trauma, grief or underlying mental health conditions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Given the complexity of the issue and the hazards it causes, the Government has been taking an inter-agency approach to address the issue.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: There is a Hoarding Management Core Group, or HMCG, led by the MSO, to coordinate efforts across agencies to resolve protracted and severe hoarding cases.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Agencies adopt a concerted approach combining enforcement efforts with community and social interventions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Together with community partners, we have made some progress in reducing the severity of many hoarding cases.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: However, some cases remain protracted and unresolved because it is difficult to gain hoarders' cooperation to declutter.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Frontline officers face real tensions on the ground, in balancing between the person's right to choose how they want to upkeep their own home and their neighbours' enjoyment of their own residences.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Officers often need to engage and persuade the hoarders repeatedly, to obtain their cooperation to declutter.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Despite our best efforts, there are cases where hoarders refuse to cooperate.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Even if their homes were successfully decluttered once, the clutter may recur as habits do not change quickly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is necessary to protect public health and safety.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: If the order to address hoarding is granted by the CDRT, then CROs will be authorised to enter the unit in question, remove and dispose of any hoarded materials and/or items that are causing unreasonable interference and take any other actions a specified by the Court.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: As Minister Edwin Tong mentioned, we will start the pilot within the HDB estate of Tampines Town.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We will, therefore, need to test it, refine it and then test it again.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The pilot will allow us to assess how the model could be scaled up in a sustainable manner.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Tampines was chosen, as it has an average caseload compared to other towns in Singapore, which will give us a representative setting in which to test the model.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: As part of the pilot, we will also look at directed mediation as an early lever, to arrest and resolve the dispute upstream, before they worsen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We hope that more disputes can be addressed early, between neighbours and with the help of agencies and grassroots leaders or GRLs, if needed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: If residents are unable to resolve the conflict by themselves, in many instances, they will reach out to GRLs and frontline agencies, such as the HDB, for assistance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: By and large, GRLs and frontline agencies are able to resolve most cases through informal mediation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This should and will continue to be the case going forward.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: However, as mentioned by Minister Tong, we will give selected frontline responders an added tool of directed mediation, to bring neighbours together to discuss their differences.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We hope this approach will help to bring even more cases to an amicable resolution.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: MND, MCCY and MinLaw consulted extensively on the enhancements to the CDMF and, in particular, the CRU framework.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In the course of our consultations, many members of public expressed strong support for the CRU.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Some have even asked when the CRU can come by their unit and conduct enforcement on their neighbour.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: So, let me end with a few points.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We recognise that enforcement tears at the fabric of neighbourly relations and should be reserved only for serious cases.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: When neighbours are engaged in a dispute, our priority must always be to bring them together, to understand each other's perspectives, needs and interests, and to cooperate on a solution that is workable for all sides.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It is neither desirable for community spirit nor sustainable for the Government to step in to resolve differences between neighbours all the time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I call on all Members to help us with this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: When your resident comes to you and says that his next-door neighbour is making noise, please, advise him to speak to his neighbour first and encourage them to go for mediation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: If these basic strategies do not work, then the case might be a severe or prolonged one.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: CRU would be alerted by HDB or other frontline officers handling the case.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Our officers could: move the case towards mediation; make investigations leading to the issuance of warnings, abatement orders or even mandatory treatment orders down the line; or help to make eventual CDRT proceedings smoother with the evidence that they have collected.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Ultimately, the CRU must not function as a first resort.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It is intended to complement and not substitute the interlocking system of positive community norms, good neighbourly relations and amicable dispute resolution through friendly discussion and compromise.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I also call on Members to continue supporting MSO's ongoing efforts with our partners and agencies to build pro-social norms that contribute towards harmonious living.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: These include: the MSO's "Love Our 'Hood" Youth Challenge for youths to transform their creative ideas into effective solutions to create a better living environment; and HDB's Singapore's Friendly Neighbourhood Award, where we recognise and celebrate the efforts of Singaporeans who have gone the extra mile to connect with and care for fellow residents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: When we have strong community norms that value harmony and reinforce considerate behaviour in the neighbourhood, fewer cases of community disputes will arise.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: And where they do arise, involved parties will be more likely to resolve their differences through mediation without prompting.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Which means less reliance on intervention through CRU or other agencies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is an outcome worth working towards even though we know it takes effort and time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: (In Mandarin):   The establishment of the Community Relations Unit (CRU) is an important step in resolving neighbourhood disputes and is a new initiative by the Government.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Through this smaller-scale implementation, we will firm up CRU's concept of operations before expanding it island-wide.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Evidence gathered by CROs through their investigations can be useful in the CDRT proceedings, saving manpower, resources and time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It is important to note that while the CRU plays a crucial role, it is not a panacea.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Communication between neighbours is necessary and cannot be replaced.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We must retain the community's ability to resolve disputes on their own.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: After the Bill is passed, we will continue to draft subsidiary legislations and further refine our operational processes.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: At that time, the then-Minister for Culture, Community and Youth, Mr Lawrence Wong, said that the Community Disputes Resolution Bill 2015 proposes to introduce a new statutory tort for private disputes between neighbours.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: He stressed that there is a need to strengthen our approach to managing such disputes.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: He emphasised individual and community ownership, and how everyone has the responsibility to be a considerate neighbour so that residential living will be more pleasant for all.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: When problems arise, residents should first seek to resolve the matter amicably with their neighbour, failing which, they should try mediation.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I had voiced my concerns as a Member of Parliament (MP) about the many cases of disputes between residents about noise, about encroachment of space, about littering and so on.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: But despite the many cries for help from the residents, there is hardly anything that the authorities can do to resolve such disputes.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: At that time, many MPs hoped that the CDR Act could help parties resolve their differences.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Unfortunately, it seems that the number of complaints that I receive as an MP has not come down.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I still see many Meet-the-People Session cases and still receive many emails about the same issues of noise, hoarding, encroachment of common space and then, people whose cigarette smoking affects their neighbours and so on.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Many MPs in this House have also raised queries about similar issues and they have asked about the effectiveness of the Community Mediation Centre in resolving disputes.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: MPs like Mr Liang Eng Hwa, Mr Louis Ng and former-MP Ms Lee Bee Wah, spoke frequently about their residents complaint about how second-hand smoke affects their resident's health.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: The media has also reported various cases about neighbours from hell and how the noise from an inconsiderate resident staying at Punggol Central had driven six families away.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: There was another reported case about a resident in Pending Road who had to tolerate hammering sound and loud lion dance music in the middle of the night.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Thus, I welcome the amendments to this Bill as it would allow the Government more levers to resolve neighbourly disputes which have a negative impact on the community.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: In fact, when the Bill was introduced in 2015, I had called on the Government to set up a Neighbourhood Police Centre staffed by Police Officers who specialise in neighbour disputes.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: At that time, I had said that, "from experience, the presence of the Police is frequently very helpful as citizens respond better when there is Police presence".

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Thus, having a person in authority and, possibly, a person in uniform, to deal with difficult neighbours would be really helpful in persuading unreasonable neighbours to be more circumspect in their behaviour.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: This is especially so, if the DG of CRU now has specific powers to issue an abatement order against a suspected individual responsible for any act or omission causing unreasonable interference.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: If they refuse to attend the mediation, the chances of resolution is zero.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: At least, with compulsory mediation, each party gets to speak up about their struggles with the noise created or the obstruction or the second-hand smoke.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I can still recall a case few years ago, my residents invited me to visit their homes to see how their neighbour's hoarding had caused obstruction to the common area.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I went down the stairs and it was cluttered by the hoarder's collection of rubbish.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: For several years, these residents suffered in silence and were concerned about the obstruction, the risk of fire and the risk of having pest infestation affecting their neighbours.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Thus, one hoarder would easily affect the living environment of four to five of their neighbours on the same floor.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: But the next day, the hoarder will simply collect these rubbish in a matter of days and start accumulating them back outside his home, inside his home.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: When I took a peep into the home, it was full of clutter with rubbish.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I do not even know how that resident got in or out of the home.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Thus, without a treatment order, the hoarding could continue indefinitely, causing grief to all the neighbours on the same floor.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: In the particular hoarding case in my constituency, the case was resolved by multiple visits by a social worker who eventually persuaded the hoarder to go for treatment for anxiety.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Unfortunately, sometimes, there are cases where an innocent resident faces allegation of causing noise when the noise may originate from elsewhere.
