speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: His neighbour may visit him multiple times or even scold him or his family.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: But I totally understand the Government's stand that they do not wish to legislate social behaviour and that disputes between two neighbours should be considered private disputes.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I believe that, for many disputes, it is a matter of being considerate for your neighbour.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Thus, the residents ought to have a discussion with their neighbours to share their concerns in an amicable manner.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: In 2019, it was reported in the media about the "neighbours from hell" in Punggol.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: They had terrorised other innocent residents for several years.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: In my view, the Police should have acted against the "resident from hell" who had harassed other neighbours unreasonably.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: It should not have been dealt with as a private dispute between two neighbours, but a public nuisance caused by one unreasonable person who has affected the public.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Like many other Members present, we all have cases that we wish to refer to the CRU for resolution immediately and we would like the CRU to be implemented and be effective as soon as possible.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I understand Minister Edwin Tong's and Senior Minister of State Sim Ann's constraints, but I do urge the Government, let us put the CRU to work as quickly as possible because all of us have many cases that we would like to refer to the CRU.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Next, Sir, I also wish to ask about the monitoring equipment or the noise sensors that can be installed to monitor the level of noise.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: The Good Neighbour Guidebook and the Singapore Friendly Neighbourhood Award are both very good initiatives.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: In 2021, in Mountbatten, I had MSO officers bringing residents together under the "Love Our 'Hood" programme to look for solutions to common neighbourhood issues and they want to encourage ownership of neighbourhood issues.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I urge the relevant authorities to keep promoting the Singapore Kindness Movement so that more and more Singaporeans will accept that it is a norm, it is a right thing to be kind, to be considerate to others and to care for one another.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: If it is in our culture to be kind and considerate to one another, then there will be fewer disputes and disputes can be resolved far more easily.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: This Bill brings in new and much needed enhancements to the framework.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I have been looking forward to this Bill for some time.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I support this Bill but I have some questions and concerns.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I know that an experimental unit will start work in Tampines.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: When is the department expected to operate at the national level covering all constituencies, just an estimate?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: On the score of matters to be covered by the CRU, Mr Speaker, I would like to seek some clarifications regarding the CRU.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Is it a request by one resident for mediation at the CMC which was rejected by the other resident, or a request to HDB to engage the neighbour which was unsuccessful?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Indisputably, noise nuisance is a very common cause of neighbours' disputes.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: However, there are many other types of disputes between neighbours.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: For example, disagreement over the placing of articles outside their homes, behavioural issues, smoking in one flat affecting another unit and so on.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Next, some clarifications on the qualifications of CROs.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I find it odd that the criteria to be a CRO, as listed in this Bill, are not by way of specified training or qualification but as long as the person holds one of the appointments specified.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Certainly, there is a whole range of public employees doing a whole range of work from clerical, administrative to operations across different types of agencies.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: So, the criteria can be more clearly defined.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I also note that the Bill proposes to give powers to the CROs to carry out a number of stated duties, such as entering residences to collect evidence, issue advisories, notices or orders and so on.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: While it is important that such entry even without the owner's approval is done judiciously and with due respect to the owner of the residence in question, on the other hand, requiring consent may, in turn, at times, frustrate or delay entry, leading to removal of evidence of nuisance creation.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: So, how will the authorities address such contending considerations?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I hope the proposed deployment of noise sensors will greatly assist with the reduction of noise nuisance.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Detection of noise and the identification of the actual source of noise are often not as straightforward as we imagine.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: A knocking noise that ostensibly comes from the direction of the flat above may well come from another flat or source and may have a different cause from what we imagine.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: During COVID-19, a persistent noise in the still hours of the night, every day, caused consternation among my residents from more than half the flats in a particular stack in a block in my constituency.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Residents spoke to their neighbours above and below their flats.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: However, the source of noise remained inconclusive after many months, with some believing later that the sound had come from a unit to the right of the units affected.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I hope the proposed noise sensors will help to improve certainty in the detection of noise and assist to eliminate or minimise noise that will cause friction between neighbours.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Will the authorities even deploy such sensors in a flat where the alleged source of noise is believed to have come from?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: If so, is consent required by the owner and what happens if the owner withholds consent?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Currently, I often hear complaints from residents telling me that there are neighbours who stop making noises after they were spoken to by HDB or the National Environment Agency (NEA).

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: But after a while, the noises will return.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Likewise, we often see feedback on high-rise littering or feeding of birds resuming after a period of deployment of NEA's cameras following earlier complaints.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I hope the Minister will ensure that there are sufficient numbers of such sensors for use for different cases.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: How would the authorities deal with recalcitrants, repeating their noise nuisance after the noise sensors have been taken off?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: What can be done to deter residents from playing the so-called "cat and mouse" game?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: He suggested that the Government should allow residents the option to have the use of noise sensors even before they proceed with mediation.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Clearer evidence of nuisance will provide a more accurate and objective focus for parties and their mediators and enhance the resolution process at CMC and thereafter.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: In many cases, there may be a number of tenants living within a unit.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I have also, in the past, received feedback on noise issues from tenants, noise arising from tenants who do shift work or work odd hours and return to their flat each day late at night or early morning or even getting up very early in the morning to go to work.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: To be fair, the tenants, whether local or foreign, who may be the subject of feedback, may be a small proportion of the total number of tenants.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I sense that this is often due to a lack of understanding on the part of the tenants that they might have subconsciously generated noises which may seem louder, especially during the quiet hours of the night.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Besides language barrier, there are sometimes practical communication difficulties trying to get through to these individuals when agency staff are often only at work during the usual office hours.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Even apart from the new provisions, I always thought that HDB can also impose obligations on owners renting out their units by way of imposing appropriate covenants at the onset when tenancy is entered into and when owners are seeking permission from HDB to rent out their units.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: In this way, owners can be better made to understand their responsibilities in respect of their tenants and tenants can also have a better understanding of what is expected of them, especially on the issue of being considerate to their neighbours.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: In the worst scenario, of course, of non-cooperation, HDB can withdraw their permission for subletting.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: The rationale for my proposal in my speech at COS last year was that, and I quote, "As mediation at CMC requires the agreed participation of both parties to a dispute, many such disputes do not stand a chance of being resolved by mediation, simply because one of the parties opts out of mediation." I have observed from my own experience with residents' disputes that as residents know that mediation is not mandatory, many would deliberately not respond to mediation.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I have also shared that notwithstanding that mediation may not always be suitable for every dispute, I have felt that for a good number of cases, it was a good opportunity wasted for parties to try and resolve their differences during mediation when parties have the option to opt out.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: However, the net can be cast wider to achieve more resolution if the requirement is not tethered to the commencement of CDRT proceedings.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I have spoken to residents who went to mediation at CMC and, notwithstanding what was agreed at mediation with their neighbours, there was still non-compliance in part or in full, rendering continuing frustrations and tensions between the feuding neighbours.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Regarding the proposed section 20, which amends the current provision of the Act allowing the application for transferring of claims from the CDRT to a Court, may I take the opportunity to just clarify with the Minister, in the case of such a transfer, will parties be allowed to appoint a lawyer to represent them, as is the case for normal State Court proceedings?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: However, if it is allowed, would this potentially lead to any injustice since parties are not allowed to engage counsel for CDRT cases and, especially if only one party is allowed to do so?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Speaker, currently, disputes between the neighbours require the residents to go to the CMC or to litigate at the CDRT, but many are reluctant to do so.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I hope that the establishment of CRU will greatly improve our process of handling neighbourhood disputes.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I look forward to the swift completion of the pilot programme and campaigns.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I further hope that the scope of responsibilities for CRU can be expanded beyond noise and hoarding issues.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I also hope that CRU can quickly expand to cover the entire Singapore, including Hougang.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I also support the amendment to mandate attendance at mediation before cases are submitted to CDRT.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: In handling many neighbourhood disputes in the past, I have encountered how parties avoid attending mediation.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I have araised this issue in Parliament before.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I believe that mandating attendance at mediation would be a very good opportunity for all parties to resolve issues.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I support this Bill. : Mr Speaker, in closing, I welcome the key changes in this Bill, in particular the setting up of the CRU, which, I hope, will bring significant improvements in the way we currently manage disputes in the community.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I look forward to the day the CRU will expand its operation to the rest of Singapore, including Hougang.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This data shows that mediation is indeed an effective method to resolve neighbourly disputes but the take-up rate, based purely on voluntary volition, has been low.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As such, I rise to support the Community Dispute Resolution (Amendment) Bill as it will encourage the usage of community mediation as a tool to resolve disputes at an early stage while empowering relevant public servants to investigate complex and hard-to-resolve cases of noise disputes and hoarding.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Notwithstanding this, I would like to raise clarifications on three aspects: one, the role of the CRU; two, some concerns about mandatory treatment order; and three, using CDRT route as a last resort.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: One of the key amendments in the Bill is the introduction of a CRU, which will provide CROs and other dedicated personnel the powers to intervene in certain community disputes and resolve cases.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: During my Meet-the-People Sessions, I often encounter residents who seek help to intervene on recurrent and perennial noise or other disturbances by their neighbours.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: What we usually do is, first, set up a house visit with grassroots volunteers helping to mediate and try to resolve the dispute between both parties amicably.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, in some instances, situations may improve for just a short period and then become recurrent again.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We will usually, then, advise the residents to further approach the CMC to seek assistance by trained mediators.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Nonetheless, given the voluntary nature of the process, most residents shared that their neighbours, whom they have disputes with, are mostly unwilling to attend the mediation.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This usually further frustrates the residents, especially the complainants, as they feel that they have no further recourse to resolve the conflicts and some remain fearful of backlash from neighbours whom they had raised complaints against.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Additionally, failure to comply with this Mediation Direction can be constituted as an offence under the law.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I am very supportive of this new initiative as it will ensure that more individuals enter necessary mediation as a course of action in resolving their disputes.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, I would like to raise two concerns.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: While I understand the need to deal with baseless complaints, I am concerned that individuals with legitimate grievances may have their cases prematurely dismissed.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Thus, I would like to ask how a fair process of evaluation of such cases will be carried out by the newly formed CRU.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: While the Bill addresses the dismissal of frivolous complaints, there is little mention of measures to safeguard the privacy and safety of individuals from being repeatedly harassed by baseless, malicious complaints.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In the same way, complainants who act in good faith may face retaliation from unreasonable neighbors whom they raised a legitimate complaint against.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This could include offering some form of legal protection to them against the other party when directed mediation process is ongoing.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Currently, in my constituency, for complex neighbor disputes of undue interference caused by individuals who are suspected to be suffering from psychiatric conditions, we involve the IMH Community Mental Health Team or the Community Intervention Teams from social service agencies to assess individuals, while respecting their privacy and require that they or their family members provide the necessary informed consent for the mental health assessment to be done.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, in our current approach, obtaining consent could be challenging.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As such, provisions in section 12A can be useful in bringing resolution to such circumstances.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Nonetheless, I believe that unless individuals become an immediate danger to themselves or others, the confidentiality of their psychiatric condition and their medical treatment rights should be duly protected and respected, even from parties involved in the disputes.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Although I understand and support the initiation of the order by the Court on an application by the DG of CRU, I would like to seek clarifications regarding the safeguards for confidentiality and protection to be put in place on residents undergoing a mandatory treatment order.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Lastly, I am encouraged by the statistics from MinLaw regarding the effectiveness of CDRT.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In this regard, I would like to ask what has been done to simplify the CDRT enforcement process and make it easier for residents to ensure non-compliance is effectively acted upon.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Speaker, I support the Community Disputes Resolution (Amendment) Bill.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This Bill encourages residents to use community mediation at the early stages of disputes and establishes a CRU, empowering CRO with enforcement and basic mediation experience to intervene and investigate such disputes.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I believe this will lead to more effective resolution of community disputes.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: During my weekly Meet-the-People Session, I often see residents repeatedly complaining about noise and hoarding issues caused by their neighbours.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Notwithstanding my considerations raised, I support the Bill.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: The Workers' Party and I support this amendment Bill.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I am asking this because there are certain groups who may feel reluctant if fees are imposed for certain reasons.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: If fees are to be charged, I request that exemptions be considered for those in need.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: The establishment of the CRU with specific powers is, indeed, necessary.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Earlier, Minister Edwin Tong and Senior Minister of State Sim Ann explained about the functions and operations of the CRU.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I hope there will be clarification on whether this CRU operates similarly to the police, where the public can contact this unit at any time, late at night or early morning, to get assistance in stopping disturbances from neighbours at that very moment.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: From what I understand, in situations where the neighbour does not agree, the party seeking compensation need to file a civil claim.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: As we know, such matters cannot be brought to the Small Claims Tribunal.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I am of the view that such issues involving neighbours are better handled by CDRT on the basis that they involve aspects and elements of neighbourliness and community relations.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Furthermore, in comparing the CDRT legal process and civil claims, the civil claims process is more complicated and challenging.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Another situation that I consider to be a neighbourhood issue is disputes involving business owners operating in commercial units located below HDB flats, which are typically found in four-storey blocks of flats.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I have been approached by several flat owners who complained that their quality of life is adversely affected by heat, odours and early morning noise coming from a commercial unit located on the ground floor of the same block.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: My complaints have been passed on to HDB and NEA several times over the years.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Most recently, a few months ago, I was approached by an affected homeowner who made a complaint and asked for help to have something done.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: The person told me that some of the neighbours who previously complained had moved to other areas because they could no longer endure the physical and mental suffering caused by the heat, odours and noise produced by the commercial unit.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: This has led to several flat owners moving to other areas to protect their health and their families' health.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I believe the new cases that I shared are also happening in other HDB housing estates.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Disputed issues often stem from a lack of awareness and understanding about the need for tolerance, mutual respect, consideration and effective communication in discussing contentious issues.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: By attending counselling sessions, it is hoped that the spirit of unity and neighbourliness can be fostered and strengthened among the parties facing disputes.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Most of us in this Chamber have received appeals from our residents for help to resolve disputes amongst neighbours.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: The most common dispute I receive, is that of noise disputes.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: In the last few years, although not in large numbers, I am seeing an increased number of appeals from residents for assistance to resolve severe or persistent noise disturbances.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Some of these cases have dragged on with no resolution, despite attempts to engage neighbours to seek mediation.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: These cases are not one-off or occasional incidences, but happen almost daily and usually late at night or in the early hours of the morning.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: The noise range from sudden loud bangs caused by objects being dropped abruptly, dragging of furniture, slamming of doors, sounds from banging of walls, loud and heavy footsteps.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Residents facing such situations have sleep disruptions and suffer from sleep deprivation.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Residents come to seek help because they are unable to resolve these issues with their neighbours, either because their neighbours deny causing the noise or do not even respond when attempts are made to engage.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: For one of my residents, the noise disturbance happens daily at night and affects his brother and his sleep.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: The situation has resulted in a worsening of their chronic conditions, including their heart condition.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: He has tried to engage his neighbour, but the neighbour denies making the noise and after approaching the neighbour, the noise has instead got louder!

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: He and his brother are finding it unbearable to continue living in the flat as they cannot get proper rest each day.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: They are prepared to sell their flat despite only recently moving in to the unit and having spent quite a large sum to renovate the flat.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: As they must fulfil their Minimum Occupation Period, they do not have the option to sell or move out of the flat and must continue to live in such conditions detrimental to their health.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: For another household, the noise disturbance they face is affecting their sleep and impacting their concentration at work.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: They have tried to engage their neighbour and, again, the noise persists.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: A few weeks ago, another resident came to see me at our Meet-the-People Session for help.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: The issue she is facing is sudden door slamming that happens in the middle of the night.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: She shared that this happens several times through the night and has been going on for quite some time.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: I was shocked, because when I looked at her, her eyes were really black and she had rings around her eyes, clearly the result of lack of sleep.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: In all these cases, attempts were made to reach out to their neighbours for an amicable solution.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: However, their neighbours denied making the noise and HDB's help was also sought to assist, but the source of the noise was not easy to determine, especially as it happens late at night or in the early hours of the morning.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Residents were advised to go to CMC for mediation.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: If their neighbour does not agree to the community mediation, they have the option, of course, to take the case to CDRT.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: The problem for many of my residents is that they do not feel comfortable escalating the case to CDRT because they feel that taking the legal route will be too confrontational and will make the situation even more complicated.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: I will discuss two areas in my speech today.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: For many of the cases, I have shared, the other party does not respond to mediation or refuses to attend mediation.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: This strengthening of the mediation process will ensure that neighbours attend mediation, the collection of objective data if needed and require the parties to take appropriate action to resolve the noise situation.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Once registered, the settlement, as the Minister has said, will give more bite to the order and it must be complied with.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: This will give more weight to the mediation process.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: With the proposed strengthening of the mediation process, I am glad that CDRT continues to be the avenue of last resort.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: This is currently the case, as cases to go to CDRT must have gone through the mediation process first and had fail to be resolved.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: I do, however, have some clarifications regarding the amendments to CMC, the new CRU and CDRT.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Will the proposed enhancements to the mediation process and framework, that is, mandatory mediation and, if mediation settlement is reached, registration of the settlement with CDRT, be effective immediately to all cases attending mediation, if the Bill is approved?

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Will the enhanced CDRT processes and powers be available for current CDRT cases?

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: I hope that the proposed enhancements to the mediation framework and the work of the new CRU will provide learnings and insights on neighbour disputes and resolution, especially noise disputes.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: In densely-populated Singapore, most of us live in high-rise homes, both public HDB flats and private apartments in condominiums.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: With the insights from CRU and the strengthened mediation and CDRT process, I hope that it will give better understanding of how to manage noise in daily living in high-rise homes and the causes of noise disturbances in such living conditions.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: With a better understanding of the causes of noise disturbances, hopefully, this can better inform those living in high-rise homes and lead to empathy and consideration from all parties.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Insights gleaned will also guide HDB and private developers in the design and types of materials to use to minimise noise between units in high-rise apartments.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: So, I hope the insights will be made available to the relevant parties.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: While like the others in the House, who have asked for the expansion of the CRU to be able to handle other severe cases, unlike others, I am actually hoping that we do not have to scale the CRU too much.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Are bonds amongst neighbours in our communities so broken that we now need to resort to having the Government step in to resolving neighbourly noise disputes?

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: I do not think so, as I regularly witness many examples of strong and healthy relationships amongst neighbours.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: While the proposed amendments strive for effective dispute resolution amongst neighbours, with the hope of building a stronger, more gracious and harmonious home for all in the community, it will require all of us to continue to work on strengthening our bonds in the community and friendships amongst neighbours.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: This will help facilitate issues getting resolved early amongst neighbours and not develop into long standing disputes.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: There is a role for CMC, CRU and CDRT for the exceptions; and I say exceptions and severe disputes, but we must not let it become the avenue for all neighbour disputes.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: In HDB estates, the usual route for dispute management has been to activate HDB or the Town Council, thereafter to recommend mediation.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: If mediation is not possible or does not succeed, then parties end up in Court namely the CDRT, where some residents end up frustrated and distressed when their cases were dismissed because they did not have the “solid evidence” that the Court required.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: It is clear that the existing procedures are inadequate.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: It is also clear that the enhanced CDMF will be a resource-intensive exercise, requiring standby teams after office hours and active management of difficult cases by the new DG of community relations.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: As there are many MPs speaking on this Bill, I will be succinct.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: But there are three particular features of the Bill which I find useful.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: First, there are avenues for quicker intervention on the ground.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: These avenues include measures such as the DG of community relations issuing abatement orders, and the CDRT being empowered to issue interim orders.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: These can be very useful when urgent action is needed to manage the ground situation.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: On this, the MCCY acknowledged in its August statement that “sound recordings made by complainants are often not useful for the purposes of determining the volume (as playback can be distorted) or source of noise”.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Senior Minister of State Sim Ann touched on this point earlier as well.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Several of my residents will be vindicated to hear this official acknowledgment that it was not their fault that they could not come up with the necessary evidence to prove their cases at the CDRT.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Thirdly, greater responsibility will be placed on landlords to manage noisy tenants in the proposed section 10A.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Indeed, it is quite common to receive complaints of noise nuisance from units which are sublet.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: It seems fair to place more responsibility on landlords who are earning rental income when their neighbours suffer.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: That said, I would like to raise three queries about the Bill and its implementation.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Likewise, I have the same question as the others.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Is there a timeline for the CRU to be rolled out nationwide?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I can think of a few chronic cases in my ward where the CRU could potentially make a big difference and a wait of several years will be hard to explain.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: A sub-question relating to the CRU is about its officers, from Director to the ground.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Will these persons be full-time and focused only on CRU work, or will they be double hatting with other duties?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Whether they are full-time, or double hatting will affect their capacity to work on dispute cases.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: There is a significant change to the CDRT regime in clause 21 of the Bill, regarding the award of costs in CDRT cases.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Earlier, Minister Edwin Tong touched on this point.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The current position is that costs will generally not be awarded to parties in CDRT cases.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: This non-award of costs makes sense, as parties generally present their own cases at the CDRT where lawyers are not allowed.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Under clause 21, this is being amended to generally permit the award of costs and disbursements in accordance with the Rules of Court.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Could the Minister further elaborate on the rationale for this change?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Will this change somehow allow, for example, a clawback of the costs incurred by the CRU to manage a case?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: More generally, I wonder what range of costs is being envisaged to be awarded and whether this will be punitive to the losing party.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I am quite worried about the scenarios that could play out under this new power of HDB.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Suppose, for instance, an adult child of a family has mental illness, and shouts and bangs doors at odd hours, thereby interfering with the neighbours’ peaceful enjoyment of their homes.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: It is foreseeable that the neighbours may take action and complain to the CRU, which then issues abatement orders to the household.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: If the required history of non-compliance is chalked up, HDB may be empowered to act under the new section 63(o) of the Housing and Development Act to compulsorily acquire the flat.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: This is a drastic measure, as the Senior Minister of State acknowledged earlier.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: If their flat is still not fully paid up, the situation will be compounded.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Will HDB assist them to find and afford their next home?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: As part of our constituency work, it is not uncommon to encounter disputes among residents ranging from noise complaints, storage of personal items along HDB corridors, second-hand smoke and surveillance or harassment.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The CDRT was set up in October 2015 as part of our Community Dispute Management Framework.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Therefore, since COVID-19 hit, how many more cases have been filed with the CDRT each year?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: One common complaint from residents is the loud and rowdy activities by neighbours at night, whether from a house party or playing the piano, during sleeping hours.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: To a university student, that might mean midnight.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: To those of us in our 40s and 50s, that might mean 10.00 pm.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: But to young parents with newborns or toddlers, sleeping hours could start even earlier at 9.00 pm or even 8.00 pm.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: While I am sure most Singaporeans are considerate and do not go out of the way to disturb others' sleep, such misalignment in expectations can cause understandable frustration.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Some countries, like New Zealand, have quiet hours when noise levels must be kept below a certain level.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: A similar benchmark might help to prevent some of these noise-related squabbles from arising.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: At the same time, we should also be conscious of over-prescription and the importance of some give-and-take.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: For example, where personal items stored along HDB corridors do not cause any fire or other hazards, I believe that the authorities have also not strictly enforced the official "no storage" rule.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: One helpful development I have noticed on the ground is the creation of Telegram or WhatsApp chatgroups for a particular HDB Build-To-Order (BTO) estate or for a particular block.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: A resident can highlight any issue in real-time, even including excessive noise from common areas like the estate's basketball and badminton courts, which will elicit approving or disapproving responses from other neighbours.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: My only concern is whether any moderating is required so that no single resident will feel bullied or isolated. : Mr Speaker, despite the enhancement of the CDRT’s powers and procedures in this Bill, I am glad to note MCCY’s position that the CDRT should remain an “avenue of last resort” and that we will further encourage the use of community mediation to help neighbours reach an amicable resolution.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: One such move is to enable the certain specified persons to direct the disputing parties to the CMC or any other mediation organisation for mediation.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I note that the new section 13M states that such specified persons “may” direct, which suggests that there is still a discretion.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I have cases ongoing in Toa Payoh East, with long-standing nature of dispute that lasts 10 years and ineffectiveness of previous mediation attempts, unwillingness of both parties to compromise have led to such long instances.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: More recently, in Toa Payoh, we have quite a number of seniors staying alone, and some have come to me to seek help because of noise disturbances, and despite their efforts to talk to their neighbours, it has gone on for quite a while and it has affected their sleep and health.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I think some Members have mentioned this as well.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The question is the fact that some of them have come to me to seek help to move house despite staying in Toa Payoh for so long.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: So, such efforts of mediation, I think, is very important.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This same discretion that CDRT already has today after a claim has been commenced is actually something that I ought to mention.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In my view, parties should generally be compelled to attempt mediation unless there is a very good reason not to.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: What are the reasons for the more than 70% of cases which fails to proceed?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: As I mentioned earlier, the amendments also make it necessary for a party to obtain either a certificate of mediation to show that he or she has attempted mediation, or a certificate of waiver of mediation showing that mediation is unsuitable, before he or she can start a claim for unreasonable interference with the CDRT.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Who can issue the certificate to certify that mediation is unsuitable for a particular case?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I think some Members have already asked when will the year-long pilot in Tampines commence?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I will reiterate the same points again, whether other areas can be covered?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I think I will reiterate those points again and I think the Senior Minister of State is probably going to hear this from the next few Members.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: For the pilot programme, may I ask the Minister, how many CROs and ACROs will be appointed?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Is that calculated by a percentage of the resident population and by local area divisions, and what would be their terms of appointment?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In particular, would the appointment be for a fixed duration and would the CROs and ACROs receive additional remuneration or allowance for taking on this new appointment on top of their current job scopes?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: While CROs will either be police officers, public officers or statutory body employees, ACROs may be an auxiliary police officer or an individual who has “suitable training” to properly exercise the powers of an ACRO.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Importantly, may I clarify if the Minister contemplates the appointment of grassroots leaders as ACROs at some future time?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In my Toa Payoh East constituency, there are a good number of older HDB blocks that have smaller flat types, narrower corridors and stairwells.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: From time to time, my grassroots leaders and I have had to visit some residents who have accumulated stuff to fill their entire unit and the adjoining common areas, usually upon feedback provided by other neighbouring residents.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I think some instances are similar to Member Mr Lim Biow Chuan's case where they are not sure how they can enter the unit.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Often, we would find that the affected resident cannot help but fall back into his or her hoarding habits, even after we have assisted with clearing up some of the stuff along with the Town Council.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Would it also be possible for such a person to be directed to undergo psychiatric treatment?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The new section 11A does not seem to provide for that.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Is there any form or template that the notice or advisory should be in?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: For the resident alleged to be hoarding, what recourse does he or she have when confronted with a CRU application for a CDRT order to declutter his or her unit?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The first step should always be to proactively build neighbourly ties and encourage consideration for one another, by encouraging residents to step out of their homes to personally befriend others that share the residential estate and space.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: When disputes occur and they are unavoidable from time to time, especially when staying in an HDB flat and you are too close to one another, dialogue and engagement on all sides should be facilitated.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: And I am most grateful for the People's Association staff and volunteers for facilitating that all these years, in Toa Payoh East and in other constituencies, even without the enhanced community dispute resolution powers in this Bill.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Intransigent neighbours who engage in abusive behaviour, littering, hoarding, vandalism and noise pollution have long been a serious issue at the municipal level.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Even if such cases are relatively few in numbers, they have a profound impact on victims.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Affected neighbours may feel an overwhelming and deep sense of helplessness at their neighbours who are engaging in ungracious behaviour.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Since 2015, we have established the CDRTs to create a specialised process to resolve community disputes.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: CDRTs are used as a measure of last resort to resolve community disputes.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: However, some will choose to ignore or flout CDRT orders.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The enhancements made in this Bill can help to address some of these concerns, as it seeks to tighten the Act and provide more effective tools for dispute resolution.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This new provision is drastic but necessary to enforce compliance.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It underscores the importance that we place on good neighbourliness and harmonious community relations in a densely populated society.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: While we support this provision as an absolute last resort, we would seek clarifications from the Government to ensure that there will be appropriate checks and balances in the enforcement of this provision.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: But what if both offences were met in relation to the same incident?

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If the flat is compulsorily acquired in such a scenario, the offender may not have been given sufficient latitude to fully appreciate the gravity of their offence under the law.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I seek more clarifications from the Minister on how this provision will be judiciously enforced, especially in cases where the root of the issue may lie in a lack of understanding of the law due to educational or mental health challenges.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Next, the Progress Singapore Party would like to seek assurances from HDB on the formula for compensation.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The policy also ensures that flat owners who infringe the rules will not enjoy undue financial gains." Would compensation for flats compulsorily acquired under clause 36 of the Bill be similarly determined?

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I would also like to highlight the provisions in the new section 13K, which empowers the CDRT to dismiss complaints deemed vexatious or made in bad faith.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I would appreciate if the Minister could provide examples of such cases or include more detailed descriptions of these terms in subsidiary legislation.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Will there be appropriate legal training for CDRT officers to make such determinations?

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Furthermore, when such complaints are dismissed, does the complainant have any recourse?

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If not, what safeguards are in place against possible abuse by CDRT officers?

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It encourages a more conciliatory approach before invoking the powers of the Tribunal.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It is also important for the CDRT to put in place systems to avoid or minimise situations where CROs handling these cases happen to live in the same block or nearby blocks and may know the parties involved.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This could potentially create situations of perceived bias, especially given the limited ability to appeal many classes of orders.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In closing, while this Bill is tough, it provides necessary measures to tackle issues that have disrupted the lives of many residents.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It gives voice and power to those who have suffered at the hands of recalcitrant neighbours.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: However, the use of severe measures must always be tempered with fairness and sensitivity to the unique circumstances of each case.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: As such, I hope that the Minister will take the opportunity to clarify some of the points that I have raised and provide the necessary assurances that these new powers will be exercised judiciously and with due respect to all parties involved.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair at 3.45 pm.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Sitting accordingly suspended at 3.24 pm until 3.45 pm.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: In a densely populated and diverse society like Singapore, harmonious living is crucial.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: The proposed amendments should make conflict resolutions faster and more robust, ideally reducing the need for formal legal actions.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: While these powers aim to help CROs address disputes swiftly, I would like to seek further clarity on the aspects of this new role.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: If CROs are drawn from existing enforcement roles, how will this complement their current responsibilities?

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Could this potentially increase their workload, and if so, what measures will the Government take to ensure that service levels remain consistent with these added duties?

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Second, as CROs will be handling complex disputes that may not always involve clear regulatory breaches, could the Ministry clarify the specific training they will receive?

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Given the sensitive nature of cases involving vulnerable groups, cultural practices, or longstanding neighborhood disagreements, will CROs be trained in de-escalation techniques, cultural sensitivity and empathetic communication?

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Additionally, could their training include community engagement methods to help them foster peaceful resolutions and address conflicts with the understanding needed to promote harmony within our communities?

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Next, I seek clarification on the limits of the discretionary powers granted to CROs.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: What safeguards are in place to prevent misuse of these powers and how will consistency be maintained, especially in minor cases that could escalate if not handled properly?

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Clear oversight mechanisms would help address concerns raised, ensuring that CROs operate within a well-defined framework.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: On the topic of mandatory mediation, I support the Bill’s emphasis on mediation as a means to preserve relationships and reduce hostility.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: If respondents do not engage meaningfully, claimants may be left without any effective resolution and may result in more friction instead.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: If the intent was indeed to narrow the scope, could the Ministry elaborate on the reasoning behind this change?

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Understanding this would help clarify the Bill's approach to handling different types of disputes.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: It is good that the Bill defines specific types of "unreasonable interference", as this provides clearer guidance for handling disputes.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: However, to ensure consistency, objective standards may still be necessary.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Without them, the definition could remain open to subjective interpretation, potentially leading to inconsistent outcomes.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: For example, in cases of noise disturbances, would the Ministry consider introducing sound thresholds or time-based guidelines?

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Establishing such standards could help reduce misunderstandings and foster peaceful coexistence.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Singapore’s religious diversity is a great strength, but it requires careful handling of disputes involving religious practices.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: While this Bill provides mechanisms to address these issues, there may be room to further strengthen provisions for inter-religious conflicts.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Singapore’s existing platforms, such as the Inter-Racial and Religious Confidence Circles (IRCCs) and the Inter-Religious Organisation (IRO), play a valuable role in fostering interfaith harmony and understanding.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: To strengthen these efforts further, could the Ministry consider formalising a mediation framework that leverages these groups specifically for disputes with religious undertones?

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: By providing structured support in the mediation process, we could ensure that culturally sensitive disputes are managed with greater consistency and formal recognition, thereby fostering mutual respect and understanding across our communities.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: While I support this provision, I would like clarification on what constitutes "compliance" in managing such disputes.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Specifically, to what extent are landlords expected to intervene and what protection is available for those who make genuine efforts but cannot resolve the issue?

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: A clear framework outlining reasonable steps for landlords would provide both clarity and fairness, ensuring they are not penalised for situations beyond their control.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: With that, I give my full support to the Bill.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It is unfortunate that we need to introduce an amendment Bill to empower Government agencies with additional regulatory tools to resolve community disputes.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: While these are necessary to bring relief to some long-suffering residents, it is a reflection and indictment of our community.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We must intensify our public education programmes and outreach to remind all residents to be more considerate towards their neighbours as we live in a high-density environment.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I support the proposed changes to direct residents to make use of community mediation as early as possible to resolve their disputes.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, there is still an important role for our teams of dedicated grassroots leaders and volunteers to mediate in community disputes.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In addition to fixing physical problems, such as hoarding and noise pollution, these teams also work closely with the IRCC to help resolve disputes which may threaten religious and racial harmony.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For cases of noise disruptions, even with the assistance of noise sensors, resolving such cases may remain challenging for the CRU to be set up.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: What is acceptable and reasonable to one may not be acceptable to others.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Tolerance levels with respect to the volume of the noise, frequency and timings vary with different people.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It is also interesting to note that the units in between have no issue with the noise travelling.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: My final point is regarding the number of cases involving mental health illnesses.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: With our rapidly ageing population, we will have more cases of mental illness related to ageing, such as dementia, in addition to cases in our general population.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: How will we retain the volunteer mediators and prevent them from burning out on the job?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As for those ordered to seek treatment for their mental health issues, how can we ensure that they will remain compliant and sustain their treatments and medications?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Do neighbours have effective and expedient recourse if they refuse to be compliant?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Actions against them may also hurt the rest of the family.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: What support is there to assist such family members in dealing with difficult and uncooperative mental health patients?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We need to encourage better cooperation and build more tolerance, while being more considerate and sensitive to the needs of others.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: On this note, I would like to conclude with my support for the Bill.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: In discussing legislation to resolve community disputes, it does stir some unease in me but the reassurance from the Ministers is something I appreciate.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: On one hand, a structured legal framework for community dispute resolution is helpful.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: It ensures protection of individuals – in terms of their rights to a comfortable personal living space and to safety in their place of dwelling.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: It lends equitability in access to justice and also halts any potential escalation and protraction of neighbourly conflicts.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: However, on the other hand, we must be vigilant against being overly reliant on legislation as a tool of resolving community disputes and we continue to encourage social responsibility and good neighbourly behaviours.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: As mentioned by the hon Minister earlier is not a silver bullet.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: At its extreme, the hardened legislation potentially and paradoxically risks polarisation and adversarial relationships in our communities and our neighbourhoods.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Inadvertently, if not handled or framed well, it could leave us with lesser room for flexibility, to give and take, to have informal dialogue as well as to partake in negotiation or mediation processes at the level of community.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Even as the Ministry proposes this Bill, it bears reminding that we must always consider that an underpinning premise of this Act is to ensure a reasonable and timely resolution of community disputes before they get worse, that this Bill is but one small part of our greater collective effort in fostering social cohesion and that we are resolute in wanting to protect what is reasonable, what is fair and just neighbourly conduct for our communities.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: I have queries and comments which I hope the Ministry would be able to clarify.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: I gather there have been challenges in addressing the issue of hoarding in our estates, to the extent that such behaviours could present as physically dangerous to others, pose a fire hazard and confer public health or hygiene concerns.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: In enacting this proposed amendment to the Act, understanding the challenges on the ground will reassure the House that there is indeed sufficient need to grant powers to the assigned community relations officer to enter a place of residence, with or without consent, for the removal of hazardous hoarded items.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: This new section, in my view, presents as a shift towards greater intervention from the authorities against the backdrop of the individual's right to choose how they wish to upkeep and maintain their own home.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Where it has been assessed that there are sufficient grounds to intervene, I am in support of this particular amendment.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: I wish to register my concern over the introduction of this section.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: The MTO has only previously been used under the auspices of sentencing after a crime has been committed, from which it was assessed that there was a strong contributory link between the criminal conduct and a person's mental illness.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Hence, as part of the crime sentencing framework, the person is mandated to seek treatment under the Criminal Procedure Code, or CPC.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: If it is the case that the mentally disordered person is so unwell and clearly so requiring mental health treatment as well, can the intent of granting access to treatment for this person be circumscribed under the existing provisions of the Mental Healthcare and Treatment Act, for example?

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: I can understand and appreciate that the MTO is intended to close the loop and take a further preventive approach on the issue, in that a person who exhibits hoarding behaviours or other behaviours of neighbourly concerns on account of mental illness, needs to be treated and it will be better for him or her.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: However – and I say this with much respect to the elected Parliamentarians here, the variety of challenges that their residents face and the various complaints that they regularly receive on the ground, in the context of a community dispute and before any crime is committed – I wonder if the inclusion of an MTO through this Bill stretches the argument past the need for public and social justice and encroaches into what could be well within a person's autonomy to decide on treatment for him or herself.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: There are indeed many people, Mdm Deputy Speaker, who have mental or physical illnesses, who choose not to be treated for their ailments for a variety of reasons.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: As a medical practitioner, it is something that I neither condone nor encourage, but I think we should be circumspect of the limits of intervention in the case of community disputes.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: I do look forward to the responses from the Ministry.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Requests for disputes resolution has been in greater demand, especially for noise disturbances and encroachment in common areas.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This seems to be done only as a last resort, available at one of the stages within the processes of the CDRT.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I am concerned that it may be costly and burdensome for a resident or household to pursue such proceedings at the CDRT.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: For cases where the underlying issue could be mental health-related, access to mental health support at the mediation stage may lead to a more expedient and effective resolution.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Hence, I would like to ask if the mediator can be empowered to make recommendations or referrals to mental health resources, if parties agree to explore mental health support at the mediation stage?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: If so, can the Government then consider providing such mental health resources at no cost for the initial consultation?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: What are the measures that can address similar problems faced by private estate dwellers, particularly for severe or egregious cases where the outcomes of mediation or CDRT are difficult to be enforced?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: On the costs framework and consequences for non-attendance at mediation, ideally, neighbours should come together to discuss how to resolve their disputes, whether it is noise, second-hand smoke, littering, hoarding or cluttering.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: However, this is not possible for some cases, due to uncooperative residents or some underlying issues, including mental health problems.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: For those in financial difficulties, monetary penalties in terms of a costs framework may be unaffordable for them.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: On the other hand, a complainant wishing to resolve the matter may not be able to afford pursuing it to the CDRT stage.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: For such situations, could measures be put in place to support greater intervention by agencies or empower grassroots leaders to help push for mediation to take place?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: (In Mandarin):   For those in financial difficulties, monetary penalties in terms of a cost framework may be unaffordable for them.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: On the other hand, a complainant wishing to resolve the matter may not be able to afford pursuing it to the CDRT stage.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: For such situations, could measures be put in place to support greater intervention by agencies or empower grassroots leaders to help push for mediation to take place.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: (In English): In conclusion, I support this Bill, as the effective resolution of community disputes will require all parties to play their part, and this will hopefully lead to a more gracious and considerate society in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The Bill also lends weight to the mediation process by introducing mandatory mediation.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This will give much needed teeth to the CDMF.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
text: The Bill aims to enhance our framework for addressing severe neighbourly disputes, particularly those involving noise and hoarding.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
text: Data from the CMC indicates that neighbour disputes have been on the rise since the COVID-19 pandemic began.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
text: By enhancing powers to address the most disruptive disputes, this Bill will reaffirm a resident's right to quiet enjoyment of their home and demonstrate our commitment to community harmony.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
text: Before I address three areas of potential concerns, I would like, however, to thank the Ministry for providing updated information about the Bill.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
text: The information provided was useful and comprehensive and it is clear that significant thought has gone into the content of these updates.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
text: The deployment of noise sensors within private dwellings raises questions about the balance between dispute resolution and the privacy rights of residents.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
text: I seek clarifications on what safeguards will be in place to ensure collected data is used strictly for the intended purpose.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
text: The Bill grants the CRU powers to act in "severe" cases, however, what constitutes "severe" must be clearly defined to prevent potential misuse of these new powers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
text: I ask the Minister to provide more detail on how this threshold will be set and consistently applied.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
text: It is crucial that their use remains proportionate to the dispute in question.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
text: I seek assurances on what checks will be in place to ensure that the CRU responds in a manner that does not unfairly penalise those it seeks to sanction.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
text: While I welcome the Bill's intent to better address severe neighbourly disputes, I have concerns about potential duplications in the process.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
text: The introduction of a new CRU, alongside the existing CMC, raises questions about how complaints will be navigated and the justification for maintaining two separate entities.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
text: For the average resident seeking redress for a disruptive neighbour, the process of where to lodge a complaint, how cases will be assessed and allocated between the CRU and CMC, and the relationship between these bodies is not clearly articulated.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
text: This lack of transparency risks causing confusion and potentially delaying much-needed resolution for those affected by excessive noise or hoarding.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
text: I seek clarification on how these different approaches will be coordinated.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
text: To ensure the changes in this Bill are truly effective in supporting those affected, it is important to streamline the process and clearly communicate to the public how they can most easily access the help they need.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
text: I am concerned that requiring neighbours to actively register an outcome, places an additional burden on them and risks uneven compliance.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
text: Would the Ministry consider automatic registration to ensure all agreements carry legal weight?

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
text: Without it, we risk inconsistent outcomes if only registered agreements are enforceable.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
text: To truly support those affected, agreements reached through mediation must carry the full force of law.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
text: Automatic registration provides greater protections and a clearer deterrent against non-compliance.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
text: However, I seek clarification on the proposed approach to address hoarding cases, particularly those involving individuals with mental health challenges.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
text: Beyond the removal of items, what actions can be taken against the hoarder or their landlord?

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
text: Are supports in place to help individuals with mental health issues that contribute to hoarding behaviours?

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
text: Would clause 13 apply in these situations and could respondents with mental health challenges be ordered to comply with resolution directives?

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
text: To effectively address hoarding, we must balance enforcement with compassion and consideration for underlying mental health factors.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
text: While I understand the intent behind section 12A, I have concerns about mandatory psychiatric treatment being ordered for individuals involved in neighbour disputes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
text: How will the need for such treatment be determined and by whom?

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
text: What measures will be in place to protect confidentiality and prevent potential discrimination?

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
text: What mechanisms are in place to ensure that affected parties are provided with independent legal advice and with information on their right to appeal or dispute any orders?

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
text: It is crucial that any approach to mandatory treatment is balanced with the rights and well-being of the individual involved.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
text: We must ensure that the focus remains on resolution and rehabilitation, rather than stigmatisation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
text: I seek clarification from the Ministry on how these considerations will be addressed in the implementation of this provision.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
text: Given the unique challenges of managing neighbour disputes, I suggest that the Ministry consider providing training in restorative justice methods and principles to all CRU officers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
text: Restorative justice focuses on collaborative problem-solving and repairing harm, which can be highly effective in resolving disputes and improving community relations.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
text: In the UK, housing associations are increasingly using restorative practices to address neighbour disputes, such as noise nuisance, verbal abuse and harassments.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
text: This includes direct mediation and conflict resolution between the offender, victims, their families and the community.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
text: By involving all parties, restorative justice can help rebuild relationships and establish shared community norms.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
text: Ensuring officers are adequately equipped to manage these complex issues in a nuanced and compassionate manner is crucial.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
text: With that consideration, what other preparation will officers receive to address the challenges they will encounter, such as supporting individuals with mental health conditions or navigating cases involving hoarding?

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
text: Ensuring a multifaceted approach that balances justice with compassion is key.
