text: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked for data on cases where settlement agreements were breached while Mr Derrick Goh asked how the CMC will maintain the high quality of its community mediation services.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In fact, it has been doing so since we conceived of the idea behind CDMF, knowing that one day, such as today, and one day when we operationalise it, we will really need to step up the mediation resources.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Currently, there are 16 satellite mediation venues right across Singapore at selected Community Clubs, ServiceSG centres as well as at Neighbourhood Police Posts.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Virtual mediation, as I mentioned in my speech earlier, is also available and in the right cases, has been very useful because you do not really have to leave the comfort of your own homes but, at the same time, you can take part in a proper mediation session chaired by a trained mediator.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We will continue to do more where we can.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked why not have evening sessions as well.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Well, in the past, the CMC did offer mediation on weekday evenings.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But the take-up rate was low and we had to deploy more staff to deal with that.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, we decided not to have those and, instead, focus our energies on offering mediation during office hours on weekdays and on Saturday mornings.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: On promotion of mediation, CMC has been highlighting the benefits of mediation through multiple channels.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: From the speeches I have heard from Members, you would do well as ambassadors for us as well as you go out there and meet your own networks and in your own community, please tell them what a mediation is about.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It is non-binding, you do not have to agree if you cannot find a set of terms that you agree with.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But at the same time, it is an opportunity to canvass your ideas constructively with the counterparty and explore different ways of finding a solution.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We have also been promoting mediation through digital and bus stop advertisements and light-hearted social media platforms and videos.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The CMC's brochures are also translated into the vernacular languages to ensure a broader and a wider reach.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: On caseload, this is expected to increase once directed mediation is operationalised.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: These duty mediators have also undergone training and they will continue to grow its pool of volunteer mediators through recruitment and appointment.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We hope that, with directed mediation, more parties will come forward for mediation.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I would add that many cases that come to CMC are settled and we will continue to track the settlement rate.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Although I did say earlier that once you have compulsory or mandatory mediation, you might expect to see a drop in those rates.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We do not have access to this data because parties do not usually report every breach of a settlement agreement with CMC.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In the spirit of community self-help, we leave it to the parties to decide what next steps ought to be if and when a settlement agreement is breached.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Preferably, parties should try to come back to the table, agree on a revised set of terms that works for both.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Sometimes, it is a breach because circumstances have changed so it may well be useful to renegotiate or maybe even have a subsequent mediation before the mediator.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Relatedly, Mr Derrick Goh also asked about the mechanics to prevent abuse of CMC services.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: For instance, an applicant cannot apply for mediation against the same respondent, within a certain period of time.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked why over 70% of registered cases do not proceed to mediation.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In many cases, parties declined or failed to respond to the mediation invitation and without speculating, it is for a whole variety of different reasons.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In other instances, parties just did not show up at the mediation sessions, despite repeated reminders.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But once we have directed mediations, we expect that to change.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Dennis Tan asked about the use of noise sensors to collect evidence pre-mediation.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Ms Sim Ann had responded to it, but I want to just add that, really, the intent of mediation is to facilitate a consensual open amicable discussion and not so much focused on what precise evidence one has and you can imagine, if you get into a mediation and one party turns up with noise data, you would expect that the other party would also want to have a series of other evidential provisions that will help to substantiate his or her case as well and before you know it, from a mediation process, you end up getting into an adjudicatory process, which is what we want to avoid.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We want it to be designed upstream, to be purely mediation and if you cannot work that through, then there are provisions downstream, which provide for the adjudicatory process to take place Mr Gan Thiam Poh asked about CMC's efforts to retain its volunteer mediators and to prevent burnout.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: CMC has, over the years, refined a robust framework to ensure that its volunteer mediators are looked after, well-managed and taken care of.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: For example, cases are carefully assessed for complexity and assigned to mediators with the commensurate requisite skill and knowledge and experience.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: There is a comprehensive training and mentorship programme that CMC has in place.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: CMC also regularly engages its volunteer mediators to seek feedback on whether they are well-supported, what else can we do, do they see areas in which they need more training in and which we will then organise and so on, to provide for a more resilient and more knowledgeable and, as far as we can, more up-to-date group of mediators.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: More importantly, the community of CMC volunteer mediators has over the years built up a strong esprit de corps.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Many of our volunteer mediators have been with us for decades.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In fact, we just had an occasion few weeks ago to appreciate them and we saw many handled large numbers of cases over many, many years and there is a very strong sense of community amongst the mediators.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: They know they play an important role in not just mediating a difference, but they see it as a higher calling to promote and preserve community cohesion and that is a very important and useful way to frame the work that they do.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: They also take it upon themselves, the more senior ones, to train and mentor younger mediators.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I can see that there is a real sense of pride in being a CMC volunteer mediator.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Whilst mediation is suitable and effective for many, I would say, most of the disputes, there will, nevertheless, be situations where mediation may not be suitable.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: CMC has worked closely with the frontline teams to guide their assessment and, in some cases, make the right call on the right types of cases.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum's question about the roles of CMC and CRU.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: CMC continues to provide mediation services whilst CRU is set up, essentially, with a range of investigatory and enforcement powers to intervene in the manner that the Senior Minister of State Sim Ann had outlined and myself as well in my earlier speech.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But we provided for CRU even at that stage to refer cases to mediation, because we feel that unless you have really intransigent cases where the issues are deep-rooted and really dug in, otherwise mediation should still be something that we think about constantly in the whole spectrum of resources to offer to the parties.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Mark Lee, Miss Rachel Ong and Mr Alex Yam asked what the consequences are if a party does not comply with the Mediation Direction or if he or she is uncooperative.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It only requires you to turn up for a mediation with your neighbour who is often someone you see on a day-to-day basis anyway and if you do not want to see him face-to-face, as I said, you can go online and do it on a virtual platform.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: More importantly, I would encourage those who are asked to attend mediation to not just go, but go with an open mind.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Try and see it from your neighbour's perspective, understand the issue.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: If you do not have a mediated solution, you really have to go for an adjudicatory position and, today, you might succeed in your claim.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: You might be able to put your shoes a bit closer to your neighbour's homes and so on; or play your music a bit louder or a bit later and so on.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But the shoe might be on the other foot at some point in time and it is not healthy for two neighbours who live in close proximity to have to live by what a third-party adjudicates or directs for you to do.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, it is really best for this to be done on a consensual, amicable basis.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Notwithstanding all of that, if there are valid reasons for not attending, either you fell ill or for some reason – there is a good enough reason – CMC will arrange for another session.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The stance of the CMC is to try, not so much catch out people who failed to come for mediation and then say that you are in breach, but to try to be on the front foot, to accommodate parties as much as possible so that they can attend the mediation and find a long-lasting solution.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Various Members have raised questions on mental health.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The Senior Minister of State Sim Ann outlined our approach to mental health earlier.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: As far as possible, we will facilitate assessment and treatment in a consensual environment.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We understand the sensitivities that Dr Syed Harun talked about and that is a very important consideration.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We want to do it as far as we can with the cooperation of the individuals; and as far as we can, also with the strong support of the family and their caregivers.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But addressing the root cause of the problem will not only mitigate the disturbance to the community, but I believe, also overall improve the quality of life for that individual and his family and also allow the community to find a more long-lasting solution.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: For example, we encountered a case where a family of two brothers played loud music, shouted and dragged furniture around, over the course of 30 years – this is a real case – into the wee hours of the morning.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The neighbours really did not want to escalate this case, did not want to take action, did not want to go to the CDRT and chose to tolerate the noise for as long as they could because they suspected that the brothers had a mental health condition.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But this also meant that the community and those around them continued to suffer this disamenity.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In such a case, CRU may bring in community mental health teams to try to secure the brothers' cooperation to be referred to for mental health assessment and support as early as possible.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But as a measure of last resort, if all else fails and this continues and disamenity and the interference continue, CRU may, then, initiate an application to CDRT and, thereafter, in the appropriate case, apply for an MTO.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: A few questions touched on increasing access to our mental health services ecosystem.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This was discussed in a different forum previously and Members can refer to those debates.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I want to emphasise that this is not really so much a Bill to deal with the mental health aspect of the case but, rather, to look at mental health as being one cause of community interference and how we address not so much the mental health issue but the community interference question.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Ms Joan Pereira asked if CMC mediators can refer parties for mental health support in appropriate cases.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: CMC mediators are trained to detect basic mental health issues, and do refer parties for mental health support if they consent.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Coming to the MTOs, I believe I have covered this in some detail in my opening speech.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But I heard Dr Syed Harun's speech, and I think it bears emphasising our thinking and our approach to MTOs in this case.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In particular, Dr Syed Harun asked why we are introducing MTOs outside of the criminal regime, the criminal context.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Currently, the breach of a CDRT special direction or exclusion order, is already an offence.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Upon conviction, as Dr Syed Harun noted, it is possible for the criminal Court, at that stage, to make an MTO and require the offender at that stage to undergo psychiatric treatment.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In other words, after there has been a breach, and after an offence has been found.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: If the root cause of the issue is not tackled early on, the person might eventually face more serious criminal charges for breaching the special direction.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We do not think this is desirable, especially if upfront, we are, at least, based on the framework that we have set out, able to discern.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And I think, most Members would agree, that in serious hoarding cases, you would most likely be able to discern that mental health conditions are at least one contributory factor to the interference.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, we believe that if we can treat the root cause early on, upfront, without bringing the person through the criminal process, and in the process, possibly stigmatising him and the family even more, then as far as we can, we should.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I would add that the enactment of an MTO framework outside of the criminal framework that Dr Syed Harun spoke about is not new.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Similar frameworks exist today under the Protection from Harassment Act and under the Women's Charter.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Dr Syed Harun also asked if the MTO framework will continue to apply if a person with a psychiatric condition is no longer causing unreasonable interference to his neighbour.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It does not apply to a person who is not causing this interference.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, even if there might be a mental disorder, but there is no nexus to an unreasonable interference being caused, then the provisions do not apply.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Patrick Tay asked about the duration of treatment that can be ordered under the MTO.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: As part of his report to the CDRT, the appointed psychiatrist will recommend the duration based on his professional judgement.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Patrick Tay and Mr Alex Yam asked about individuals who are unable to afford CDRT-ordered assessment or treatment.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I would say this to Members, psychiatric assessments ordered by the CDRT are conducted at no cost to the individual.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I would also add that no Singaporean will be denied access to appropriate treatment due to his inability to pay.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: When the appointed psychiatrist does his assessment, he will also consider that individual's financial ability to pay for the treatment and this will be assessed against the available financial support measures, such as inpatient subsidies, MediShield Life, private health insurance and MediFund.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh asked how we can ensure compliance with mental health treatment ordered by the CDRT.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The starting point is that the MTO will be regarded as a Court Order under the CDRT and must be complied with.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: On the ground, healthcare workers will of course do their best to support the individual in complying with these orders.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In general, they will follow up with close case management monitoring and this is mainly through telephone calls or home visits to ensure that the patients attend their outpatient reviews and comply with the treatment regime including medication, and if need be, patients will be referred to other agencies and community outreach teams for further social support.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Mark Lee asked if the scope of what constitutes "unreasonable interference" in section 4(2) of the CDRA has been narrowed.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Although clause 3(f) of the Bill appears to introduce a new definition of "unreasonable interference", the Bill does not actually change the existing definition of "unreasonable interference" in section 4.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The new definition inserted under clause 3(f) is a legislative drafting technique that merely makes it clear that the current definition in section 4 applies whenever the term unreasonable interference is used in the Act, especially in the new Part 2A.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: To be clear, the CDRT will have jurisdiction to hear and determine cases involving the full range of acts and omissions that may cause unreasonable interference with a neighbour's enjoyment or use of place of residence.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: As for the CRU, for the reasons that I have set out earlier, and which Senior Minister of State Sim Ann has expanded on, CRU will focus its resources on severe neighbour noise and hoarding cases.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, when it comes to mediation, what I have explained earlier in mediation cases, we want it to be as broad as possible and give the unit as much flexibility as possible to determine what noise, what hoarding might be and what disamenity might be and the different constituent steps that might lead up to it, so that there is more flexibility for it to do its work, as I have explained in my opening speech.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Faisal Manap asked about whether disputes related to ceiling leakages can also be brought under this scheme.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It is possible for the CDRT to hear such a dispute if there is evidence that the leakage stems from an act of unreasonable interference.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The affected resident can also consider bringing the claim to the Strata Titles Board if the issue in question happens on strata title properties.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But I would caution against attributing the increase solely or primarily to just the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Hybrid work arrangements, work from home, could be one factor, but there may be a whole range of other factors that have contributed to this increase.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: For example, there could be greater awareness of the CDRT, with cases being reported in the news over time.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Seventy-five claims or 9% of them, are involved a complaint on obstruction of place of residence and 67 claims or 8% of total claims are on excessive smoke.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It is possible for a single claim to contain allegations on more than one type of unreasonable interference, but it is quite clear that the vast majority of claims revolve around excessive noise.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Ms Ng Ling Ling and Mr Alex Yam spoke on simplifying the CDRT process.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We agree and we have tried to do so in this Bill.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: CDRT processes have been designed to be simple and accessible for users, and claimants and respondents do not require legal knowledge to pursue or defend a claim.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The forms are in plain English and they are accompanied by explanatory notes that guide users through the filing process.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: CDRT judges play a proactive role in not just leading, but also guiding the proceedings.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: For example, the judge will pose questions to the claimant or respondents directly in order to elicit a position from them and also ask them, guide them, to provide certain pieces of evidence to support their claim.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The CDRT is also not bound by the rules of evidence that ordinarily apply to court proceedings, so it can consider any evidence that points towards the source of interference, the type of interference or its intensity and surrounding circumstances.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: To alleviate the evidential difficulty, we have, as I have explained earlier, put in place processes to integrate upstream CRU findings so that we do not have to repeat the evidence gathering.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We understand that despite all these, some users may still find the process to be daunting and complex and it is foreign to many parties to be engaged in an adjudicatory court process.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, detailed step-by-step guidance on the CDRT process has been made available on the judiciary's website.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Members of the public can also approach the State Courts directly for process-related queries.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And for those who wish to seek advice on their legal options, they can approach Pro Bono SG's various Community Legal Clinics.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: They will be very happy to advise on the options available as well as on the process.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng, Mr Mark Lee and Miss Rachel Ong asked about the enhancements we are making for tenant-occupied properties under the new section 10A.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I touched on it in my opening speech, so I will just briefly respond.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It just makes it faster, neater because you are now before the CDRT and we want to ensure that the landlord is aware that there is such a case happening, rather than to wait for one breach and then the next step before involving the landlord.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, we brought the landlord's bond upfront and at the first stage.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The landlord must be given express notice of the tenant's actions and it is therefore not that the tenant or the landlord is unaware.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In this context, I think Members will agree with me that the landlord really should not be sitting back and doing nothing.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Inaction on the landlord's part, it does not gel with our philosophy of having a community-first approach that we are trying to foster.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Miss Rachel Ong suggested that we enhance the deterrent effect of the compliance order.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: At the same time, Mr Yip Hon Weng expressed the view that expectations must be balanced and realistic, and Mr Mark Lee referred to the need for a framework that provides clarity for the landlords.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The different speeches on this topic itself illustrates the competing tensions that we see and we have tried to adopt a calibrated approach.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We are aware that there is a range of profiles of landlords – some are more cooperative than others, some are more hands-off, some may even be living overseas, as Mr Yip highlighted.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We will take on board Mr Yip's suggestion when we operationalise these enhancements and provide clear guidelines to landlords to help them understand the obligations – a point that Mr Mark Lee made as well.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Really, the last thing we want is to inadvertently create disputes out of this process when we are trying to resolve an underlying neighbour dispute between two parties.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I believe Mr Dennis Tan suggested introducing an additional factor on subletting by having covenants imposed before allowing a landlord to rent out or to sublet.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I think, as I have said, finding the right approach with the right balance is useful and we do not think at this stage, we want to impose or have an additional factor on the ability of a landlord to rent out as long as this process is in place.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Derrick Goh and Assoc Prof Razwana Begum asked whether mediated settlement agreements can be registered as a CDRT order by default instead of by consent.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Because if every settlement agreement were automatically registered or had the same effect as a Court Order, this would change the complexion of mediation, which is consensual and amicable.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And it may well hinder parties from wanting to come forward to enter into a mediation agreement.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Requiring consent makes also for a more transparent process.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It crucially helps to preserve the trust between the settling parties.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: If both parties agree, then it can be registered and both will go in with their eyes open, rather than having it automatic.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This process of having consent also aligns with our position in the Mediation Act.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Under the Mediation Act, any party outside of community disputes who reaches a mediated settlement agreement, also registers it by consent under the Mediation Act.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Miss Rachel Ong asked about the agreements between a resident and a Government agency.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The CDMF is concerned with disputes between neighbours and we do not expect a Government agency to be a party to such a dispute.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Dennis Tan asked about the transfer provision, whether lawyers will be allowed in CDRT cases that are transferred to the Magistrates' Courts or the District Courts.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The short point is that under section 20, the reason for the transfer is because a party may well file a claim that includes claims or allegations that fall outside of the CDRT's jurisdiction.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, in such a case, the CDRT court or judge will decide to transfer the case to the appropriate Magistrate's or District Court.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In such cases, the ordinary civil process will apply and both parties may engage legal representation if they wish.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Ms Sylvia Lim asked about the cost provision that we are trying to put in.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, now we are introducing it to align with the usual cost practices.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The intention is like other cost orders in court.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It is at the court's discretion to reflect the fairness and equity of the particular situation.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: As I said in my opening speech, if a party unreasonably refuses to attend mediation, even before the Mediation Direction kicks in, when your neighbour offers to go to mediation and you unreasonably refuse to attend, leading to protracted proceedings, in such a situation, the court might then consider that it is appropriate to order costs consequences to be visited upon the party refusing to attend.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Or sometimes there could be a flagrant disregard of agreed obligations, for example, in a breach of a settlement agreement, or there is a dishonest conduct of the proceedings, withholding evidence or making false statements and so on.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Ms Jessica Tan asked if the CDRT enhancements will apply to existing CDRT cases.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This really depends on the enhancement in question.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: As I said, we have a pilot in the CRU but not a pilot in the other cases.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But where possible, we have tried to ensure that the existing cases will benefit from the enhancements in this case.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But there are some cases where you are halfway through the process.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Ms Tan might want to look at the interim arrangements, the Interim Orders clause, as well as the registration of settlement agreements provision.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: These will kick in after the Bill is effective because you do not want to introduce a provision halfway through a process when the parties are already engaged in the system.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Derrick Goh asked for us to monitor the CDRT's effectiveness.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We will certainly do so and continue to make enhancements as may be necessary.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I want to start this conclusion by thanking the team of officers across all three Ministries who have worked over several years in coming up with this piece of legislation.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It has not been straightforward, mainly because it is not just dealing with a process or a procedural issue, but you are really deeply intervening with two neighbours, the way in which they live their lives, the way in which they conduct themselves as neighbours.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And so, we had to be very careful about striking the right balance, as I emphasised in my speech earlier.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But at the same time, we realised that disputes between neighbours, sometimes they have a religious undertone, sometimes there is an ethnic undertone, and if left unchecked, they can escalate very quickly.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It is very easy to label these disputes as one type or another and that is really unhelpful, but those labels sometimes stick.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This then frays our relations, undermines our trust and disrupts our social cohesion.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: That is not something that we want to see.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In reality, while this is a Bill that deals with the process, sets up a framework, deals with mediation, I really think that this is a Bill that is aimed squarely at trying to enhance our social cohesion in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We want to do this to ensure that there is a framework, people know what the framework is, but at the same time are able to practise self-moderation, knowing what the framework is, and having the ability themselves to self-help, to sort out their own problems.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Which is why I have emphasised, whether it is the CDRT or the CRU, we do not want to be overly intrusive and we want to retain a balance and discretion and a responsibility on the part of neighbours to live in harmony and to sort out their own issues from time to time.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Fundamentally, we want to strengthen trust amongst our communities.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We can then elevate this level of harmony to strengthen our national multicultural inter-faith harmony as well.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: That really was the thinking behind a very detailed root and branch review of the CDMF.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Between you, Minister, and Senior Minister of State Sim Ann, 80 minutes of clarification.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Are there more clarifications for the two Ministers?
